root_cause.text: The IMA filesystem code unconditionally accesses the `hash_algo_name[]` array using `crypto_id` values without validating that the index is within bounds, causing an out-of-bounds read when `crypto_id` is set to `HASH_ALGO__LAST` for unsupported TPM hash algorithms.
root_cause.evidence: The patch shows that when `ima_tpm_chip->allocated_banks[i].crypto_id` is initialized to `HASH_ALGO__LAST` for unsupported TPM algorithms (like TPM_ALG_SHA3_256 with ID 0x0027), the code in `create_securityfs_measurement_lists()` directly uses this value as an index into `hash_algo_name[algo]` without bounds checking. The KASAN report confirms a global-out-of-bounds read at `hash_algo_name+0xb8/0x420`. The fix adds an explicit check `if (algo == HASH_ALGO__LAST)` to use an alternative naming scheme (`_tpm_alg_<ID>`) instead of accessing the out-of-bounds array element.

The KASAN report confirms a global-out-of-bounds read at `hash_algo_name+0xb8/0x420`. The fix adds an explicit check `if (algo == HASH_ALGO__LAST)` to use an alternative naming scheme (`_tpm_alg_<ID>`) instead of accessing the out-of-bounds array element.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add boundary check for HASH_ALGO__LAST to prevent out-of-bounds array access and use TPM chip allocated bank IDs for filename generation when algorithm index reaches the sentinel value.
intent_record.what: Added conditional logic to handle the special case where algo == HASH_ALGO__LAST by using TPM chip allocated bank algorithm IDs instead of hash_algo_name array lookup. This pattern is applied twice: once for ascii_runtime_measurements file naming and once for binary_runtime_measurements file naming.
intent_record.how: When the algorithm index reaches HASH_ALGO__LAST (a sentinel/boundary value), the code now formats filenames using ima_tpm_chip->allocated_banks[i].alg_id in hexadecimal format instead of attempting to access hash_algo_name[algo], which would be out of bounds or invalid. This prevents potential buffer overruns or invalid memory access while enabling proper naming for TPM-specific algorithm banks.

This is the exact fix needed to prevent the unconditional array access vulnerability described in the root cause.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 9fa8e76250082a45d0d3dad525419ab98bd01658
Author: Enrico Bravi <enrico.bravi@polito.it>
Date:   Fri Apr 12 11:09:53 2024 +0200

    ima: add crypto agility support for template-hash algorithm
    
    The template hash showed by the ascii_runtime_measurements and
    binary_runtime_measurements is the one calculated using sha1 and there is
    no possibility to change this value, despite the fact that the template
    hash is calculated using the hash algorithms corresponding to all the PC
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in the `create_securityfs_measurement_lists()` function. At lines 460-461, the code unconditionally accesses `hash_algo_name[algo]` using `algo = ima_algo_array[i].algo` without validating that the index is within bounds. The loop iterates from 0 to `securityfs_measurement_list_count`, which is set based on `NR_BANKS(ima_tpm_chip)` and potentially incremented if `ima_sha1_idx >= NR_BANKS(ima_tpm_chip)`. However, there is no bounds checking to ensure that `ima_algo_array[i].algo` produces a valid index for the `hash_algo_name[]` array. If `ima_algo_array[i].algo` is set to `HASH_ALGO__LAST` (for unsupported TPM hash algorithms), this would cause an out-of-bounds read. The code does not validate the returned `algo` value before using it as an array index in `hash_algo_name[algo]` at lines 463 and 469. Additionally, in `ima_measurements_show()` and `ima_ascii_measurements_show()`, the `algo_idx` is used to access `e->digests[algo_idx]` without bounds validation, though the primary vulnerability is in the file creation where `hash_algo_name` is accessed without bounds checking.
